items.title: Frozen-slow explicit Euler with fast microsteps
items.statement: Given autonomous fields f and g, a state (x,z), macro step H>0, and integer m>=1, set h=H/m, update x once by explicit Euler, freeze x through m explicit Euler updates of z, and return (x+,z_m).
items.strategy: Definition: specify inputs, domain, all slow and fast updates, failure statuses, field-evaluation and coupling-data counts, and state that no wall-clock speedup is promised.

references.title: Michael Günther and Adrian Sandu, Multirate Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations, CSL-TR-25-5 (2025)
Michael Günther, Numerical Analysis and Simulation I — Ordinary Differential Equations, Chapter 4: Multirate Schemes (lecture notes, 2017/18)

items.title: Synchronous Picard waveform relaxation on a finite window
items.statement: On a window [0,Delta], apply the integral fixed-point map simultaneously to both continuous state waveforms and return the current pair and a finite-budget status.
items.strategy: Definition: specify the waveform space, integral map, admissible ball/contraction preconditions, stopping test, budget exhaustion status, and exact evaluation convention.

references.title: Ekachai Lelarasmee, The Waveform Relaxation Method for Time-Domain Analysis of Large Scale Integrated Circuits: Theory and Applications, UCB/ERL M82/40 (1982)

items.title: Block variation bounds for a frozen-slow Euler step
items.statement: If F=(f,g) is bounded by M on a tube and U is an exact path there, then ||U(t)-U(s)||<=M(t-s); every frozen-x fast microstate z_j also satisfies ||z_j-z_0||<=j h M.
items.strategy: Use the Volterra equation and vector-integral norm bound for the exact path; apply the algorithm recurrence and induction for the fast microstates.

references.title: Michael Günther, Numerical Analysis and Simulation I — Ordinary Differential Equations, Chapter 4: Multirate Schemes (lecture notes, 2017/18)
Mark Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Lecture 34: Global Analysis of One-Step Integrators (2016)

items.title: One-step stability of frozen-slow Euler with fast microsteps
items.statement: If F is jointly K-Lipschitz on a set containing both successful runs' inputs and fast microstates, the frozen-slow/micro-Euler one-step map is Lipschitz with factor 1+L_T H, where L_T=sqrt(2K^2+2K^2 exp(2KT)); the bound is uniform in m.
items.strategy: Derive a two-block nonnegative error matrix, unroll the fast microstep recurrence, bound its entries by K exp(KT), and use the Frobenius norm to obtain 1+L_T H.

references.title: Michael Günther and Adrian Sandu, Multirate Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations, CSL-TR-25-5 (2025)

items.title: Second-order global bound under symmetric coupling and a cubic defect
items.statement: A symmetric exact-flow macro composition with a time-reversal-symmetric coupling interpolant has global order two if, independently, it satisfies a uniform O(H^3) exact-start defect bound and a (1+LH) one-step stability bound on a common tube.
items.strategy: Treat the composition as a one-step method and apply the global one-step error theorem with p=2; symmetry is not used to infer the defect bound.

references.title: Michael Günther and Adrian Sandu, Multirate Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations, CSL-TR-25-5 (2025)
Mark Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Lecture 34: Global Analysis of One-Step Integrators (2016)

items.title: Contraction and finite-sweep error bound for synchronous waveform relaxation
items.statement: If F is K-Lipschitz and M-bounded on a closed radius-R ball about the initial state, Delta M<=R, and q=K Delta<1, then the synchronous waveform Picard map is a self-map contraction and k sweeps satisfy ||U^k-U*||_infty<=q^k||U^1-U^0||_infty/(1-q).
items.strategy: Prove the constrained waveform set is a nonempty closed subset of the complete continuous-curve space; show map invariance and contraction by the vector integral norm inequality; apply the constructive Banach theorem and pass its geometric tail bound to the fixed point.

references.title: Ekachai Lelarasmee, The Waveform Relaxation Method for Time-Domain Analysis of Large Scale Integrated Circuits: Theory and Applications, UCB/ERL M82/40 (1982)
Mark Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Lecture 34: Global Analysis of One-Step Integrators (2016)

items.title: Local defect bound for frozen-slow Euler with fast microsteps
items.statement: For a jointly K-Lipschitz field bounded by M on a common set containing the exact path and all microstates, exact start gives a frozen-slow/micro-Euler macro defect at most 4 K M H^2.
items.strategy: Split the defect into slow and fast coordinates. Bound the slow integral by K M H^2/2; bound each fast integrand mismatch by 3 K M H and integrate over the macro window.

references.title: Michael Günther and Adrian Sandu, Multirate Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations, CSL-TR-25-5 (2025)
Michael Günther, Numerical Analysis and Simulation I — Ordinary Differential Equations, Chapter 4: Multirate Schemes (lecture notes, 2017/18)

items.title: Fixed-time first-order error bound for frozen-slow Euler
items.statement: For a jointly K-Lipschitz field bounded by M on a common set containing the exact path, all macro states, fast microstates and outputs, exact initial data gives the displayed fixed-time O(H) node error and an O(H) error for every fast microstage, uniformly in the microstep counts.
items.strategy: Derive the macro error recurrence from the local defect and one-step stability, apply batch-28's finite recurrence lemma with p=1, and use block variation bounds for intermediate fast stages.

references.title: Michael Günther and Adrian Sandu, Multirate Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations, CSL-TR-25-5 (2025)
Mark Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Lecture 34: Global Analysis of One-Step Integrators (2016)

title: Multirate and partitioned time integration — Examples

items.title: A dissipative electromechanical toy model under slow-fast blocking
items.statement: For q'=v, v'=-q-v+i, i'=v-8i, the quadratic mechanical-electrical energy is nonincreasing; at H=1/10 and m=4 the frozen-slow method from (0,1,0) returns (1/10,9/10,369/5000) using one mechanical and four electrical field evaluations.
items.strategy: Differentiate the quadratic energy, then substitute the initial state into the assigned macro update and four frozen-slow electrical microsteps.

items.title: A stable coupled model has an unstable explicit fast microstep
items.statement: For x'=-x and z'=x-8z, every exact solution decays to zero, but H=0.6, m=2, h=0.3 gives fast microstep multiplier -1.4 and one step (x+,z+)=(0.4,1.84) from (1,1).
items.strategy: Verify the explicit continuous solution and its decay, substitute the initial values into the assigned scheme, and compute the fast perturbation multiplier.

items.title: Freezing a varying slow waveform leaves a first-order coupling error
items.statement: For x'=1, z'=x from (0,0) on [0,T], the frozen-slow method has terminal z error TH/2; midpoint interpolation in each fast microstep is exact for this model for every positive integer microstep count.
items.strategy: Compute the macro recursion and finite sum for the frozen coupling, compare with the exact solution, and evaluate the midpoint-coupled alternative explicitly.
